raw_response:
I am not going to spread myself too thin this year. My land is only 4.1 mu, and with some people in the family working off-farm, I have to keep the plan steady and manageable. I still keep some cotton because I know it well and it gives me cash over a longer picking period, but stevia is what I will put more area into because in recent years it has brought decent money if the stand is good. I have middle school education, so I listen to what people say and also to the input dealer and township technician, but in the end I still farm by what I have seen on my own land. Since I have well water, I am not fully dependent on rain, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate too freely. I will fertilize in splits where it matters, especially for cotton, because one-time application is easy but not as safe if the crop comes weak later.

For stevia, I want a clean field and a strong early stand, so I will transplant on time, use enough base fertilizer, and irrigate after transplanting to help survival. For cotton, I will not chase very high input because the area is small and labor is troublesome, but I will still use a moderate fertilizer rate and watch for aphids and bollworm. I would rather spend a bit on fertilizer and one or two sprays than let the crop go backward and lose yield.
